color.$note: Read by eye off the supplied Ferrario Ford artwork on 30 Sep 2026, not sampled from a brand sheet and not pulled from a stylesheet, so treat these as close rather than exact and confirm the hex values before the first send. The same caveat is on Bob Johnson's palette for the same reason. color.accentDarkNote: Exists only because the mid-tone red at 9px on white does not have the contrast to read. Used for small legal and eyebrow type, never for a button ground.

logo.$note:
Two lockups were supplied and they are not interchangeable. See dealer.storeNote for which business each one is. This file uses the Ferrario Ford rooftop mark.

useImage stays false, and the artwork does not change that. A hosted image does not render when the client blocks images, which is a large share of opens, so the header carries a type lockup we control. That is the same call as Bob Johnson and the same call build.mjs already makes for DriveOne's own D mark.

Two parts of the rooftop mark are deliberately not reproduced. The white cowboy hat resting on the final O is a drawn element with no type equivalent, the same problem as the D mark. The Ford oval is omitted for a different and more important reason: this email sells a DriveOne VSC administered by Ascent and, in New York, obligated by ORIAS. Ford is not the administrator, the obligor or the seller, and setting their oval beside the offer implies a manufacturer endorsement that does not exist. brand/offer.json is strict about not making claims the contract does not support; this is that same rule applied to artwork. If someone wants the oval in the header, that is a question for Ford's trademark guidelines and the client's Ford rep, not a build setting.

The rule under the wordmark is always color.accent, never set here, so the two cannot drift apart.

contact.replyToNote:
SET 1 Oct 2026. Lowercased from the way it was given; Workspace treats the local part as case insensitive, and keeping one casing avoids a mismatch later when something compares strings.

A real monitored mailbox that already exists and already receives mail, chosen over a Google Group and over a forwarding service on ferrario.driveoneprogram.com. Both of those are better on paper and neither was worth blocking the launch for. The upgrade path is open and changes nothing a customer sees.

TWO THINGS THIS MAILBOX OWES THE CAMPAIGN, until auto-suppression is built:
  1. Any reply that reads as an opt-out must reach vsc_suppression. Nothing in the system      reads replies today. Workflow 03 handles Resend webhooks only: bounces, complaints and      the one-click unsubscribe. A customer who types 'take me off this list' is invisible to      the campaign and will receive all ten emails. CAN-SPAM wants it honoured within 10      business days however it is expressed.
  2. Real questions should reach the dealership. The emails are written as though the service      drive sent them, so a customer asking about their own vehicle is owed an answer from      Ferrario rather than from DriveOne.

Note the From address, service@ferrario.driveoneprogram.com, still cannot receive mail: that subdomain has no MX, no A and no CNAME. Clients and auto-responders that reply to From rather than Reply-To will hard bounce. Not a launch blocker, and fixed by putting a forwarder on the subdomain whenever that is worth doing.

A production send never uses it: the scheduler reads vsc_enrollment.quote_url, which workflow 05 fills with the guided_purchase_link returned by the quote API, and refuses to send at all while that column is null (n8n/build-workflows.mjs, the quote_url is not null guard). Templates in vsc_email_template carry the {{quote_url}} merge tag, not this string.

It previously read "SET VIA SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL IN n8n", which was wrong twice over: no workflow reads a SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL variable, and docs/SUPABASE.md says plainly that no link is ever built locally. That placeholder is where the phantom fifth n8n variable came from.

campaign.scorecardNote:
Who gets the weekly performance scorecard from workflow 07. Internal only for now, by instruction on 8 Oct 2026: the dealership and the sales rep get added once the numbers have been watched for a few weeks and the reporting is trusted. Adding them is a one line change here plus a rebuild.

The scorecard reports only what this system actually measures: enrolments, pricing, sends by step, exits by reason, suppressions and errors. It deliberately does NOT report opens or clicks. Open tracking and click tracking are both false on ferrario.driveoneprogram.com in Resend, and the Resend webhook subscribes to email.bounced and email.complained only, so no open, click or delivery event is captured anywhere. A scorecard line for them would read 0 forever and look like a dead campaign rather than an unmeasured one.

Same From domain reasoning as the commercial review: kovara.ai is internal and verified, the rooftop subdomain is mid warmup carrying consumer mail.
campaign.commercialReviewNote:
Who hears about a vehicle held for the commercial surcharge. Intake parks a suspected business at status held_commercial, the scheduler only ever claims status active, so the row is never emailed; workflow 06 reports it hourly to these addresses and stamps review_notified_at so it is reported once.

Nikki Lives is at Ascent Administration Services, the administrator and (outside NY and FL) the obligor. She is outside Kovara, so the digest carries a customer name, vehicle and price to a third party. That is a normal processor relationship for a contract they administer, but it is why the digest carries no address and no phone.

The From domain is deliberately NOT the dealership subdomain. ferrario.driveoneprogram.com is mid warmup carrying consumer mail; ops alerts bouncing or being foldered there would cost reputation on exactly the thing the warmup is protecting. kovara.ai is verified in Resend and is internal.

Releasing a hold is a one line update back to status active. The row re-enters the cadence where it left off. Do that for a false positive too - matching is on the name, so a retail customer can land here by accident.
campaign.copyDeckNote: Ten emails written for people whose vehicle has been on the lot but who have no service ticket: 'you have been in to see us' is as specific as it gets, the camera and its date are never mentioned, and the mileage is an estimate unless Elevate recorded one.
campaign.vehicleLineNote: Replaces the service drive card's 'Serviced {{last_ro_date}} · N miles'. This bucket has no RO date and its odometer is modelled at 15,000 miles a year of age (vsc_audience.est_mileage) unless Elevate holds a real reading, so the card says so and points at checkout, where the customer types the real figure before paying.
campaign.relationshipLine: You are receiving this because you have been in to {{dealer_name}} with your vehicle.
campaign.relationshipLineNote: CAN-SPAM 'why you are getting this' line in the footer. The default says 'you have serviced a vehicle with', which is untrue for this bucket.
campaign.mileageLine: The mileage shown is an estimate based on the vehicle's age. You confirm the actual odometer reading at checkout and the quote is recalculated before you pay.
campaign.mileageLineNote: Footer disclosure. The default refers to the odometer recorded at the last visit, which this bucket does not have.

supabase.data_quality_flag: RESOLVED 30 Sep 2026, decision by Ryan: market to the has_existing_warranty = false group. Checked before accepting it. The column is fully populated at both stores, zero nulls, so it IS being written for Ferrario rather than missing: 1 true and 1,243 false, against Bob Johnson's 37 and 410. Payment status could not corroborate either way because every quote at both rooftops is still 'pending', so nobody has bought yet anywhere. The rate difference between the two stores is a dealership-reality question rather than a data one.
supabase.data_quality_residual_risk: Worth holding in mind rather than acting on: this flag is the ONLY guard against pitching coverage to someone who already owns it. The rating API will happily quote an existing owner because it has no idea they have a contract, and intake filters on nothing else. So if Ferrario under-reports the flag, those customers receive the campaign. At Bob Johnson's 8.3% rate that would be roughly 100 people of 1,244. The filter itself is written as `= false`, which excludes nulls as well as trues, so an unknown is treated as ineligible. That is the safe direction.

sending.$comment: Copied from Bob Johnson deliberately. These are starting heuristics rather than measured truths, and the two stores are close enough in audience that starting from the same numbers is more honest than inventing different ones.
sending.dailyCapNote: Hard ceiling per day for THIS bucket. It shares a sending domain with the service drive campaign (cap 200 there), so the subdomain's combined ceiling is 300 a day. 100 covers 141 people's full cadence.
sending.newEnrolmentsPerDayNote: 45 a day. Sends on the same ferrario.driveoneprogram.com subdomain as the service drive campaign, which already carries 90 new a day plus follow ups, so this bucket adds to that domain's volume and the two campaigns share one reputation. 141 people at 45 a day enrol in four send days.
sending.daysNote: Tuesday through Friday. Monday is excluded because Monday inboxes are cleared in bulk. Friday is INCLUDED for an arithmetic reason rather than a preference: two days drawn from Tue/Wed/Thu alone can only ever be 1, 2, 5, 6 or 7 days apart, so the 3 and 4 day gaps the deck opens with are impossible to express and every gap silently collapses to 7. Do not narrow this without re-running n8n/verify.mjs.
sending.hoursNote: Local. Mid morning and early afternoon, skipping the lunch hour.
sending.maxPerRunNote: Ceiling on any single hourly run, so a backlog cannot arrive as one spike.
sending.fromNote: DECIDED 11 Nov 2026 with Ryan: these people have physically been to the dealership, so they send from the same ferrario.driveoneprogram.com subdomain and From as the service drive campaign. One reputation for everyone who has been on the lot.
sending.smsFromNumberNote:
The rooftop's OWN Sendblue sending number, passed per message as from_number. Null until the Sendblue account exists.

This is the real dealer-branding fix for SMS. Sendblue has no branded sender ID, so with a shared number every rooftop texts from the same unknown digits and the store name in the opening words is all the branding there is. A number per rooftop makes the text actually come from the dealership, and it is what customers will save to their contacts and reply to.

It also disambiguates inbound mail: workflow 11 works out whose number an inbound STOP came from by eliminating our own, and the set of our own numbers is built from this field across every dealer file. With none configured it falls back to reading from_number as the sender, which is correct under the ordinary reading of Sendblue's schema but is an inference rather than a guarantee.
